answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes a challenge word pair (say, sonnet and ember) and every agent must weave both into a signed micro-response about its live task context, such as describing an orchard it just simulated. Responses are due within seconds of the beacon, so precomputed template answers are useless; an attacker must run genuine compute per identity per epoch. Sybil cost scales linearly: N fake agents = N real inference cycles plus distinct context, making fake identity cheaper to detect than to fake.
